data.title: Richemont Jewellery Demand Lifts Sales, but One-Time Tariff Gains Flatter Margins
data.description:
Richemont (OTC: CFRUY), the owner of Cartier, reported stronger first-half sales on Friday, November 13, while a tariff-related gain complicated the profit comparison. Its results for the six months ended September 30 showed revenue of €12.28 billion, up 16% at actual exchange rates and 17% at constant currencies.

The latest quarter maintained double-digit growth. Reuters reported sales of €5.95 billion for the three months ended September, above the €5.89 billion Visible Alpha consensus. Sales grew 13% at constant currencies. That is a quarterly measure, separate from the 17% growth figure covering the full six-month period.

First-half operating profit rose 33% to €3.13 billion, but included €229 million of positive tariff-related one-time items. Excluding those items, operating profit was approximately €2.9 billion and the operating margin was 23.6%, compared with the reported margin of 25.5%. The underlying operating margin still improved by 140 basis points.

Gross margin tells a more restrained story. It rose 120 basis points on the reported basis, but fell 70 basis points after excluding the positive one-time contribution. Richemont said higher raw-material costs, notably gold, weighed on production costs. Stronger sales and a higher reported margin therefore do not mean input-cost pressure has disappeared.

data.title: Applied Materials Sales Jump 53%; Next-Quarter Revenue Target Tops Estimates
data.description:
Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT) reported record quarterly revenue and forecast further growth as chipmakers expand manufacturing capacity. Its November 12 results put fiscal fourth-quarter revenue at $10.41 billion, up 53% from a year earlier, for the period ended October 25.

The company expects fiscal first-quarter revenue of $11.1 billion, plus or minus $500 million. Reuters reported an LSEG analyst average of $10.89 billion. The forecast midpoint is above that estimate, although the guidance range extends on either side of it; the release does not guarantee an eventual revenue beat.

Fourth-quarter GAAP earnings were $3.40 a share, compared with non-GAAP earnings of $4.16. Reuters put the adjusted earnings consensus at $4.05. The company’s next-quarter non-GAAP earnings target is $4.35 a share, plus or minus $0.20. These adjusted figures should be compared with adjusted estimates rather than the GAAP result.

The manufacturing-equipment business supplies a different view of AI spending from the companies selling finished chips. Reuters reported that Semiconductor Systems revenue increased about 64% to roughly $8 billion. Its account also put China at 25% of quarterly sales, down from 29% a year earlier, despite growth in dollar sales there. A lower geographic share therefore does not necessarily indicate falling revenue in that market.

The new outlook points to continued equipment demand, while leaving the usual uncertainty about the timing of customer spending. It is a company forecast for the next fiscal quarter, distinct from the record revenue already reported.

data.title: Corteva Sales Fall 9% as Brazil Weakness Weighs on Its Updated Outlook
data.description:
Corteva (NYSE: CTVA) reported a 9% decline in third-quarter sales and updated its full-year outlook after conditions in Brazil proved weaker than management expected. Its November 11 earnings release gives shareholders a new look at the crop-protection business following the separation of its seed operations.

Quarterly revenue was $1.59 billion, below the $1.77 billion analyst estimate cited by Investing.com. Adjusted pro forma operating earnings were $0.06 a share, compared with a $0.10 consensus. On the company’s pro forma GAAP presentation, continuing operations recorded an after-tax loss of $54 million, against a $60 million profit a year earlier. The adjusted operating figure and GAAP loss measure different treatments of costs.

The pressure was concentrated geographically. Latin American organic sales fell 31%, as farmer financing constraints, high interest rates and stocked distribution channels delayed purchases in Brazil. Pricing competition also hurt mature products. North American organic sales grew 7%, while Europe, the Middle East and Africa rose 14%, showing that the weakness was not uniform across the business.

Corteva now expects 2026 adjusted pro forma operating EBITDA of $1.1 billion–$1.125 billion and adjusted pro forma operating earnings of $0.76–$0.80 a share. Those are management forecasts using non-GAAP measures. The release attributes the updated outlook primarily to deteriorating Brazilian conditions, while describing demand for new, differentiated products as resilient.

The reporting basis deserves attention after the corporate split. A November 10 filing says the seed-business spin-off was completed on October 1, and that additional separation-related reporting work delayed the quarterly filing. The September-quarter results are presented on a pro forma basis; they should not be compared casually with historical figures for the former combined seed and crop-protection group.

data.title: U.S. Jobless Claims Rise to 200,000, but Four-Week Average Holds Steady
data.description:
U.S. applications for unemployment benefits increased to a seasonally adjusted 200,000 in the week ended November 7, the Labor Department reported Thursday. That was 9,000 above the prior week’s revised level. The increase brought claims above the 195,000 consensus in Econoday’s survey, published by CME Group, while the broader trend changed little.

The previous week’s reading was revised from 189,000 to 191,000. The four-week moving average, which smooths weekly fluctuations, was unchanged at 195,250 after revisions. Comparing the latest figure with the originally reported prior week would therefore overstate the weekly increase.

Continuing claims moved in the other direction. Seasonally adjusted insured unemployment fell by 20,000 to 1.697 million in the week ended October 31. This series covers people receiving benefits after their initial application and runs one week behind the headline measure. The insured unemployment rate held at 1.1%; that is a different measure from the national unemployment rate in the monthly jobs report.

Econoday described the figures as consistent with a labor market showing limited activity. Its analysis notes that the four-week initial-claims average has remained below 200,000 since the week of October 3, while continuing claims remain well below 1.8 million. The latest rise in first-time applications therefore sits alongside stable or declining measures of longer-term benefit use.

For markets, the distinction matters: a single weekly increase offers a narrower signal than a sustained rise across both series. Claims help track layoffs and the income supporting consumer spending, but do not by themselves measure the pace of new hiring. Thursday’s release supplies a fresh labor-market reading without establishing a broad deterioration or determining the Federal Reserve’s next policy decision.

data.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO; Colette Kress Takes Interim Role
data.description:
Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) confirmed on Thursday, November 12 that Jensen Huang has resigned as president, chief executive and a director, effective immediately. The company’s announcement puts finance chief Colette Kress in charge on an interim basis as the chipmaker begins searching for a permanent successor.

Kress will retain her responsibilities as chief financial officer while serving as interim CEO. The board will consider candidates from inside and outside the company. She joined Nvidia as CFO in September 2013, giving the temporary appointment continuity within the existing leadership team rather than bringing in an outside executive immediately.

Directors also appointed Harvey C. Jones as Nvidia’s first board chair. The board said it expects operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap to proceed without interruption. That is the board’s stated expectation for the transition, rather than a new financial forecast.

The decision changes the position described in our earlier Thursday briefing, when directors were reportedly weighing Huang’s future and no decision had appeared in the newsroom. FOX’s report places the resignation after reports of two extramarital relationships, including one involving a woman suspected of spying for China. Those allegations provide the background to the change; the company’s transition release does not announce a conclusion to the investigation.

Nvidia kept its next financial update on the calendar: third-quarter fiscal 2027 results are due Tuesday, November 17 at about 4:20 p.m. Eastern, followed by the 5 p.m. earnings call. Its original call notice identifies the reporting period as the quarter ended October 25. The appointment resolves who leads the company for now, while leaving the permanent succession decision ahead.

data.title: UK Economy Grows 0.7% in Q3 as Services Outpace Construction
data.description:
Britain’s economy grew 0.7% in the third quarter of 2026, up from 0.5% in the previous quarter, the Office for National Statistics said on November 12. Services provided the main lift, while a contraction in construction showed that the improvement was uneven across industries.

The first quarterly estimate puts real GDP 1.9% above its level a year earlier. The 0.7% headline measures growth from the preceding quarter; it is not an annualized rate. September alone recorded 0.2% growth, after August was revised down to no growth and July remained at 0.4%.

Reuters reported that the quarterly expansion was the strongest since the first quarter of 2024 and matched economists’ forecasts. September’s increase exceeded the Reuters poll’s expectation of unchanged output. The distinction matters: the monthly figure surprised, while the overall quarterly result was in line.

Services output increased 0.9% in the quarter, compared with 0.1% growth in production and a 0.7% decline in construction. Computer programming, consultancy and related activities grew 4.4%. The ONS said some of the businesses reporting the largest turnover gains were involved in AI and cloud computing, but cautioned that its data could not quantify those activities’ exact impact.

Reuters said the release followed the Bank of England’s rate increase and upgrade to its 2026 growth forecast the previous week. Stronger activity adds to the evidence informing the next policy decision, while the split across industries matters for businesses exposed to UK demand.

The figures are an early estimate and remain subject to revision. For now, the release presents a firmer aggregate growth picture without showing the same strength in construction or every consumer-facing service.

data.title: Siemens Orders Jump 58% as It Targets 9%–11% Revenue Growth for 2027
data.description:
Siemens (OTC: SIEGY) reported a record €34.8 billion of fourth-quarter orders on November 12, a 58% increase from a year earlier, and forecast comparable revenue growth of 9%–11% for fiscal 2027. The industrial group’s outlook assumes a changed reporting perimeter as it prepares to deconsolidate Siemens Healthineers.

In its earnings announcement, Siemens said quarterly revenue rose 11% to €23.7 billion. Orders grew across all industrial businesses, with particularly strong contributions from Mobility and Smart Infrastructure. The book-to-bill ratio was 1.47, meaning new orders exceeded revenue recorded during the period.

Profit in the Industrial Business measure rose 22% to €3.9 billion, with a 16.8% margin. Quarterly net income increased 32% to about €2.4 billion. These are separate measures: the industrial-business figure does not represent consolidated net profit.

Investing.com reported that Siemens also raised its medium-term comparable revenue growth target to 7%–11%, from 6%–9%. Its report highlighted demand connected with electrification, digitalization and data-center construction, putting the results within the broader investment cycle supporting industrial technology.

The scope of the next-year forecast matters. Siemens said its fiscal 2027 group outlook excludes Healthineers-related effects, including that business’s operating earnings contributions and the transaction’s non-cash gain. Its projected earnings per share before purchase-price-allocation accounting of €10.20–€10.80 compares with €9.27 for fiscal 2026 on the corresponding basis excluding Healthineers.

data.title: Stock Market Today: Nvidia Slides as Board Weighs Huang’s Future Before Thursday’s Open
data.description:
Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) remained sharply lower before the Thursday, November 12 opening bell after reports that its board was considering removing Chief Executive Jensen Huang. Reuters reported that directors met late Wednesday to decide his future, following a Wall Street Journal report that they were preparing to oust him. No leadership decision had appeared in Nvidia’s newsroom as of 4:41 a.m. Eastern Thursday.

The reports mark a change from the board’s November 8 statement, which expressed confidence in Huang and his leadership team while announcing an independent investigation. The New York Times reported a second alleged extramarital relationship, with another Nvidia executive, according to Reuters’ account; Reuters said it could not immediately verify that report. Nvidia had not immediately responded to Reuters’ request for comment on the meeting. Yahoo Finance’s coverage also reported Bernstein’s downgrade to Market-Perform and Baird’s downgrade to Neutral.

Nvidia fell 8.61% to $158.78 in Wednesday’s after-hours session, Forbes reported. CBS News put the market-value loss since November 8 above $450 billion. The premarket decline had narrowed by Thursday’s 4:40 a.m. Eastern quotes: Yahoo showed $163.73, down 5.76% from Wednesday’s regular close, while Nasdaq showed $163.79.

The weakness extended beyond Nvidia. At 4:40 a.m. Eastern, Yahoo premarket trades showed CoreWeave (NASDAQ: CRWV) at $58.15, down 4.31%, and Micron (NASDAQ: MU) at $790.28, down 2.59%. Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) rose 3.64% to $573.05. Nasdaq’s quote feed showed $58.12, $790.01 and $573.00 respectively at the same minute, corroborating the direction and approximate size of each move. Changes compare with Wednesday’s regular close. Delayed Yahoo futures quotes timestamped 4:30 a.m. Eastern showed S&P 500 futures down 0.32% at 7,616.25, Nasdaq 100 futures down 0.66% at 28,284.00 and Dow futures up 0.06% at 52,612.

That reverses part of Wednesday’s AI-led rebound at the 4 p.m. Eastern regular-session close. CoreWeave gained 24.71% in the regular session, its strongest advance in more than three months; Reuters reported its target of adjusted profitability in the first half of 2028. The Philadelphia chip index gained 5.7%, Micron 11.9%, AMD 7.3% and Nvidia 2.9%; Seagate (NASDAQ: STX) rose about 10% and Western Digital (NASDAQ: WDC) 8.3%. The S&P 500 closed at 7,619.38, up 1.3%, taking its weekly gain to 3.3%; the Nasdaq rose 1.6% to 25,466.19 and the Dow added 254.60 points to 52,486.49. Our earlier Thursday briefing covers the closing session and earnings schedule. The November 12 daily video briefing walks through the Nvidia reports, CoreWeave rally and today’s agenda; the quotes above update its earlier market snapshot.

Asian shares also weakened Thursday. Taiwan’s Taiex closed down 2.63%, with the Taipei-listed shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM) down 2.3% and MediaTek down 3.5%, CNA reported. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng lost about 1.3%; Japan’s Nikkei fell 0.7% and South Korea’s Kospi 0.6%.

U.S. bond trading resumes after the Veterans Day closure. Weekly jobless claims are due at 8:30 a.m. Eastern, according to CNBC’s calendar. After today’s close, Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO) reports fiscal first-quarter results against its own $18.0 billion–$18.2 billion revenue outlook. Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT) reports fiscal fourth-quarter results against revenue guidance of $10.25 billion, plus or minus $500 million. These are company forecasts, not reported results or analyst estimates.

Reuters reported Wednesday that traders fully priced a December rate increase of at least 25 basis points, citing CME FedWatch. The October Producer Price Index release follows Friday, November 13, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. Nvidia’s quarterly results and earnings call are scheduled for Tuesday, November 17.

data.title: What’s Ahead for the Stock Market This Week
data.description:
After Friday’s sharp selloff triggered by President Trump’s decision to raise tariffs in response to China tightening rare earth exports, investors are starting the week on edge. The focus now shifts to trade tensions, earnings season, and the Federal Reserve’s next moves.

Big Earnings Week: Banks and Chipmakers Take Center Stage

This week kicks off a busy stretch of third-quarter results from major financial firms and tech companies.

  • Banks: JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and Citigroup all report on Tuesday, followed by Bank of America and Morgan Stanley on Wednesday. Later in the week, American Express, Truist Financial, and State Street will wrap up the financial lineup.
  • Tech & Chips: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC) reports Thursday after strong AI chip sales boosted its revenue 40% in the first half of 2025. ASML follows on Wednesday after raising concerns about tariffs and slowing demand for chip equipment.
  • Tech events: Oracle’s AI World conference begins Monday, and Salesforce’s Dreamforce starts Tuesday — both likely to bring attention to artificial intelligence and enterprise tech. Earnings Calendar >>

Data Delays and Fed Watch

The federal government shutdown, now entering its third week, is likely to delay several key reports, including retail sales, inflation (PPI), housing starts, and jobless claims. Some data will still come through, like the NFIB Small Business Optimism Index on Tuesday and homebuilder confidence on Thursday.

Investors will also tune in to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s speech on Tuesday, along with comments from Fed officials, including Michelle Bowman and Christopher Waller. The Fed’s Beige Book, which gives an overview of economic conditions across regions, will be released on Wednesday.

Market Context

Bond markets will be closed on Monday for Columbus Day (also observed as Indigenous Peoples Day), but stock exchanges will remain open.

With limited economic data and uncertainty around Washington’s budget standoff, markets are likely to take their cues from corporate earnings and Fed commentary.

In short, this week is about navigating through noise — balancing worries over tariffs and the shutdown against potential optimism from strong bank and chipmaker earnings.

data.title: What Is the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA)? A Complete Guide
data.description:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA), often referred to as the Dow Jones, the Dow 30, or simply the Dow, is one of the world’s most recognized stock market indexes. The DJIA tracks 30 of the largest publicly traded companies in the United States, making it a widely followed indicator of the overall health of the U.S. economy and stock market. Investors searching for DJIA today, DJIA futures, or Dow Jones price updates often turn to this index as a barometer of market sentiment.

But what exactly is the DJIA, what stocks does it include, and how do traders and long-term investors use it in their strategies?

What Is the DJIA?

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) is a price-weighted index created in 1896 by Charles Dow and Edward Jones. Unlike market-cap-weighted indexes like the S&P 500, the DJIA assigns weight based on a stock’s price rather than its market capitalization. This means a company with a higher stock price (e.g., Apple or UnitedHealth) influences the index more heavily than lower-priced stocks.

The DJIA is designed to reflect the performance of blue-chip companies across different sectors of the U.S. economy. It does not include utilities or transportation stocks, which are tracked by separate Dow indexes.

What Companies Are in the DJIA?

The DJIA is composed of 30 large, publicly traded U.S. companies that are considered leaders in their industries. These companies span sectors such as technology, finance, healthcare, consumer goods, and industrials.

Here’s a snapshot of the DJIA holdings (as of 2025, September 15th):

Note: The index is reviewed periodically, and constituents may change depending on mergers, bankruptcies, or shifts in market relevance.

How Does the DJIA Work?

  • Price-Weighted Methodology: Higher-priced stocks have more influence.
  • Dow Divisor: A proprietary number adjusted for stock splits, dividends, and corporate actions ensures continuity.
  • Sector Balance: While tech stocks (Apple, Microsoft) now hold significant weight, the index aims to represent the broader U.S. economy.

If Apple (AAPL) rises $5 in a day, it has the same impact on the DJIA as Boeing (BA) rising $5, even though their market caps differ drastically.

Why Do Investors Watch the DJIA?

  • Economic Barometer: The DJIA today is seen as a snapshot of the U.S. economy.
  • Historical Importance: Created in 1896, it has over 125 years of market history.
  • Market Sentiment: Widely quoted on news outlets and financial platforms.
  • Trading Opportunities: Investors follow DJIA futures, DJIA ETFs, and Dow Jones index funds for exposure.

How to Trade or Invest in the DJIA

Investors can’t buy the DJIA directly but can gain exposure through exchange-traded funds (ETFs), futures contracts, or mutual funds:

  • SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) – tracks the DJIA closely.
  • DJIA Futures – contracts traded on CME, allowing leveraged exposure.
  • Index Funds – designed for long-term buy-and-hold investors.
